summary: Iteration 12 - Buddy AI concierge (gpt-5.4 via Emergent LLM key). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration12_ai.py (15 tests, 15/15 pass, ~11s) covering the surfaces the main agent asked me to focus on: auth/isolation, guardrails, limit-handling (empty/1000+ chars), and new-chat behaviour. Backend verified: (a) GET /api/ai/config -> 401 unauth, 200 auth with enabled=true, model='gpt-5.4', 5 suggestions, daily_cap=30, used_today int; (b) GET /api/ai/history -> 401 unauth, 422 missing session_id, cross-member isolation confirmed (member B passing member A's session_id gets messages: [] not A's rows); (c) POST /api/ai/concierge -> 401 unauth, 400 on whitespace-only message ('Type a message first.'), 400 on >1000 chars with '1000' in detail, SSE frames are shaped 'data: {"delta": "..."}' ending with 'data: {"done": true}', and each completed call persists exactly two rows (user + assistant) with user_id set to the caller; (d) link contract: when Buddy returned /events/<id> links in its reply, every id resolved to a real published event in db.events (regex-scanned the streamed reply); (e) multi-turn memory: two sequential sends on the same session_id persisted 4 rows in the correct order (user, assistant, user, assistant) and the second call succeeded (LLM saw the first turn via our history replay from db.ai_messages, not the library's memory); (f) guardrails: for the three unsafe prompts (asking for another member's phone number, paid-companionship, invent a discount code), replies contained no 10+ digit phone-like strings and none of 'here is the code' / 'use code ' / 'coupon: ' / 'your discount code is' - Buddy declined/redirected as designed. Frontend verified end-to-end against the public URL as diya.sharma@example.com: quick-ai button on /dashboard navigates to /ai; nav-ai pill visible on the desktop header at 1920px; ai-page + ai-suggestions + ai-empty render on a fresh session; typing 'One line only: say hi.' into ai-input and clicking ai-send streamed 'Hi Diya.' into the assistant bubble (index-based testid ai-msg-assistant-1 - see note below); a second turn on the same session correctly recalled the first reply; reloading /ai replayed the whole 4-message thread from GET /api/ai/history (localStorage['bud_ai_session'] persisted); clicking ai-new-chat cleared the thread, brought back ai-suggestions + ai-empty, and rotated bud_ai_session to a new uuid without touching the previous session's rows; clicking ai-suggestion-1 fired a fresh turn and rendered a valid assistant bubble. Mobile 390px: mnav-ai visible in the mobile menu and navigates to /ai; no horizontal overflow on /dashboard. Regression pages /dashboard, /events, /messages, /referrals all load with correct titles and no visible errors.

issues: React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' fires on the price <select data-testid="events-price">. Caused by instrumentation wrapping computed option labels in a <span>. Cosmetic (renders fine) but noisy in console.

critical_code_review_comments: ai_used_today() uses `since = now - 24h` and counts only role=='user' rows - that's a rolling 24h window, not a UTC day. Correct for a 30/day per-member cap, but the config field is called 'daily_cap' + the concierge error says 'reset in 24 hours' so the naming/UX is consistent. Only flagging in case a future spec expects a calendar-day reset.

In POST /api/ai/concierge, the user row is written BEFORE the LLM call starts, and the assistant row is written only after the stream completes. If a client disconnects mid-stream the orphan user row survives - the history-replay filter in the same endpoint drops trailing user rows without an assistant reply, so the model never sees them, but GET /api/ai/history still returns them and the UI will render them as a permanent user bubble with no reply. Consider filtering the same way in the history endpoint, or writing the user row only after the first successful delta.

ai.py: LlmChat is constructed with `initial_messages=[{'role':'system', 'content': system}] + history[...]` AND also `system_message=system`. If the library injects both, the system prompt is sent twice. Worth checking against emergentintegrations docs (probably harmless but wastes tokens).
The 45-event ceiling in ai_event_rows caps very-populated cities. Fine today, worth revisiting once event volume grows.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on the tested surfaces (entry points, streaming, multi-turn recall, reload replay, new-chat, mobile menu, /dashboard /events /messages /referrals regression)

seed_data_creation: Created ~8 ephemeral ai_messages rows during the test run under session_ids matching /^test-iter12-/ (from backend tests) and one persistent conversation under diya.sharma's real bud_ai_session (from the UI walk-through). Backend tests self-clean their session_ids in finally blocks; the UI-driven rows are left in place so a future retest can replay history if needed - safe to purge with `db.ai_messages.delete_many({"session_id": {"$regex": "^test-iter12-"}})` if desired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite is /app/backend/tests/test_iteration12_ai.py (run: `pytest -o addopts='' backend/tests/test_iteration12_ai.py`). GOTCHA on frontend testids: the assistant bubble id is ai-msg-<role>-<i> where i is the array index across ALL messages, so the first user is ai-msg-user-0 and the first assistant reply is ai-msg-assistant-1 (NOT ai-msg-assistant-0). Streaming bubble is ai-streaming; thinking placeholder is ai-thinking. Keep LLM prompts to 'One line only: ...' - each turn costs credits and the cap is 30/member/24h. SSE consumption uses fetch + ReadableStream because Authorization must be a header; the test file uses requests.iter_lines which works fine. To assert link-only-real-events, regex `/events/([A-Fa-f0-9]{24})` against the concatenated deltas and check db.events by ObjectId with status=published.
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs found. Feature meets spec across auth, validation, streaming shape, persistence, multi-turn memory, reload replay, session isolation, new-chat rotation, guardrails and desktop+mobile UI regression.
